verses-and-rhymes-by-the-way: The writer known as Norah gathers her poems and rhymes — light verse on travel, nature, and everyday moments noticed along the way. Unpretentious and musical, the collection is the work of a gifted amateur writing for pleasure. Readers who enjoy gentle, old-fashioned poetry will find much to like.
barriers-burned-away: Edward Payson Roe's breakthrough novel unfolds against the Great Chicago Fire of 1871, which literally burns away the barriers between his characters. Through romance tested by disaster, Roe preaches faith, honesty, and the chance to begin again. The book made him famous and remains a vivid picture of nineteenth-century American city life.
wallenstein-s-camp-a-play: Schiller's Wallenstein's Camp — the lively prologue to his great Wallenstein trilogy — shows the imperial general's soldiers carousing, grumbling, and boasting. In one bustling act, the whole Thirty Years War comes alive through its common fighters. A brilliant curtain-raiser to a dramatic masterpiece.
demetrius-a-play: Schiller's unfinished final play dramatizes the mysterious False Dmitri, who claimed the Russian throne in the Time of Troubles. Though death left it incomplete, the surviving scenes show the master's power undimmed. A fascinating fragment from the summit of German drama.
if-i-may: A. A. Milne's If I May gathers his whimsical Punch essays — on holidays, heroes, and the small absurdities of life. His light touch never fails. The perfect bedtime book for grown-ups. Crickets, cousins, and railway carriages all amuse his gentle pen.
toasts-and-forms-of-public-address-for-t: William Pittenger, the Andrews raider turned preacher, offers toasts and forms of public address for all who wish to say the right thing — weddings, banquets, funerals, and public days. Model speeches show the way for nervous orators. A handbook of Victorian eloquence and good manners.
